The Q5_K Vulkan-oracle direct-F32 WMMA probe cloned the Q4/Q8 VK128 padded wave64 f16acc skeleton for the dominant RADV pipeline matmul_q5_k_f32_f16acc_aligned_l. It compiled through CMake/Ninja, selected through the direct MUL_MAT path after a Q8_1-selector ABI bug was fixed, emitted 32 static v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16 sites, and passed focused CPU-reference p512 plus p513 tail rows; p33 correctly stayed on the existing narrow rows2 route. It is rejected for production promotion because same-runner focused p512 timing regressed versus the current packed Q8_1 MMQL128 route on all Q5 rows: Kcur 866.67 -> 971.27 us, Qcur 1215.98 -> 2476.18 us, ffn_out 7191.96 -> 17643.78 us, and ffn_gate 6332.38 -> 14489.87 us. The ISA comparison also shows it is still not the RADV schedule: 20480 versus 22528 LDS bytes, 32 ds_load_b128 versus RADV's 64 ds_load_b64 plus 128 ds_load_u16_d16, and 64 versus 192 stores.

The grouped ds_read_b64 Q5_K direct-F32 WMMA probe preserves the rejected VK128 padded wave64 route shape and changes only the fragment-read window to load four A fragments and four B fragments for each k-half before issuing each 4x4 WMMA block. This mechanically matches the RADV Q5_K oracle on the 64 ds_load_b64 and 32 WMMA axes, but still misses RADV's 22528-byte LDS footprint, 128 ds_load_u16_d16, 128 LDS b16 stores, and 192 buffer stores. Focused CPU-reference gates passed for p33, p512, and p513; p33 correctly stayed on the existing narrow rows2 route while p512 and p513 selected the candidate. It is rejected for production promotion because same-runner focused timing regressed every p512 and p513 row versus current routing: p512 Kcur 887.78 -> 1046.75 us, Qcur 1232.95 -> 2471.40 us, ffn_out 7308.67 -> 17817.09 us, ffn_gate 6662.22 -> 16905.31 us; p513 Kcur 891.04 -> 964.61 us, Qcur 1594.35 -> 3375.88 us, ffn_out 9362.91 -> 23583.29 us, ffn_gate 8558.62 -> 20055.20 us. Matching RADV's ds_load_b64 count alone is insufficient; the next Q5 direct-WMMA attempt must address the remaining LDS-store/writeback/lane-ownership deltas together or return to the packed-Q8_1 path.

Padding alone does not recover the RADV coopmat schedule; the next Q4 work should stop cloning direct-F32 HIP WMMA at this level and either reproduce RADV's lower-level cooperative-matrix scheduling much more exactly or return to packed Q8_1/x4 reuse.

The prefetch route passed p512 and exact p513 CPU-reference rows while selecting the intended provider, and exact p33 stayed on the existing narrow route. Source-level prefetching changed wait placement and pressure but still did not reproduce RADV's 32-static-WMMA / 192-ds-load cooperative-matrix lowering.

It compiled through CMake/Ninja with no spills (wave32, SGPR=25, VGPR=134, LDS=20480) and emitted 16 static v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16 sites, 12 ds_loads, 2 ds_stores, 8 global loads, 64 global stores, and 28 s_waitcnts. Wave-pair output ownership alone does not recover RADV's subgroup-64 cooperative-matrix lowering; the HIP builtin still lowers as independent wave32 WMMA owners with far shallower LDS traffic.

The true wave64 WMMA probe used the ROCm __builtin_amdgcn_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16_w64 builtin rather than compiling the wave32 builtin in wave64 mode. It follows the AMD matrix-instruction-calculator RDNA3 mapping for A/B fragments and D stores, preserves the VK128 padded direct-F32 shape, and compiles through CMake/Ninja with no spills (wave64, SGPR=29, VGPR=165, LDS=20480). The generated ISA is the closest direct-WMMA match so far: 32 static v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16 sites, 32 ds_loads, 2 ds_stores, 8 global loads, 64 global stores, 155 s_waitcnts. The first implementation accidentally used a wave32 lane id in wave64 mode and failed correctness; after fixing lane ids to 0..63, both low-half and high-half OPSEL routes passed p512 CPU-reference rows while selecting correctly, and the low route passed exact p513 with exact p33 staying on the existing narrow route. It is rejected for production promotion because same-runner p512 focused perf regressed versus current MMQL128 on every row: Kcur 972.56 -> 1535.23 us low / 1503.17 us high, Qcur 3943.78 -> 8354.39 us low / 8357.47 us high, ffn_out 14110.24 -> 26927.58 us low / 27073.09 us high, ffn_gate 12483.27 -> 27026.65 us low / 26952.06 us high. Wave64 WMMA correctness and 32-static-WMMA structure are now proven, but this direct-F32 dataflow remains too slow versus packed Q8_1.

Lowering accumulator footprint alone loses because it doubles the column workgroups and likely reduces B reuse; the Q4 packed path should keep the 128-column tile unless a future schedule also improves load/wait behavior.

Padding the packed-cache rows raises LDS/VGPR pressure but does not materially improve the LDS wait schedule; future packed-path work should target actual LDS-read issue order, B-cache ownership, or instruction scheduling instead of row padding alone.

Keep it opt-in only as evidence that merely splitting B payload loads across more lanes is not the missing Vulkan parity axis.

The explicit ds_read_b64 direct-F32 WMMA probe preserved the VK128 padded wave64 shape, direct F32 RHS, and ROCm wave64 WMMA builtin while forcing A/B LDS fragment reads through inline assembly. It compiled through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=30, VGPR=169, LDS=20480, no spills, 256 ds_load_b64 sites, 0 ds_load_b128 sites, 32 static WMMA sites, 396 s_waitcnts, and 2 barriers. The route selected correctly for p512 and p513, while exact p33 stayed on the existing narrow Q4 route and passed. It is rejected for production promotion because focused p512 and p513 CPU-reference rows failed with finite error after optimizer-visible asm: p512 ERR about 0.0058-0.0115 and p513 ERR about 0.0017-0.0115 versus tolerance 0.0005. Earlier no-memory-clobber asm produced NaN/inf, so optimizer visibility matters, but direct half4 asm output, conservative lgkmcnt waits, and explicit address_space(3) base-pointer arithmetic still do not make the forced-b64 fragment feed semantically equivalent to the passing W64 route or RADV. Prior artifact before the LDS-base check: cache/hrxv1/gfx1151/q4-w64-b64asm-h4out-memclobber-20260618-011846/.

The grouped ds_read_b64 direct-F32 WMMA probe preserved the VK128 padded wave64 shape and explicit LDS b64 fragment reads, but changed the compute window to load four A fragments and four B fragments for each k-half before issuing the 4x4 WMMA block. This mechanically matched the RADV load-count axis better than B64ASM: 64 ds_load_b64, 0 ds_load_b128, 32 WMMA, 206 s_waitcnts, 2 barriers, SGPR=29, VGPR=199, LDS=20480, no spills. A no-wait grouping emitted the same 64 ds_load_b64 class but failed focused p512/p513 correctness with NaNs. The conservative waited grouping selected correctly for p512 and p513, kept exact p33 on the narrow Q4 route, and passed focused CPU-reference gates for p512, p33, and p513. It is rejected for production promotion because same-row Kcur p512 perf regressed badly versus the current MMQL128 baseline under the same runner and explicit baseline gate: 1038.69 us for MMQL128 versus 3103.19 us for B64GROUP. Matching RADV's LDS load count and 4x4 fragment reuse is therefore not enough while the HIP inline-asm wait schedule and direct-F32 WMMA dataflow remain far from the RADV cooperative-matrix schedule.

The B-oct packed-Q8_1/x4 probe mechanically brackets the only positive post-oracle Q4 packed-path axis. It preserves the accepted MMQL128/B-quad dataflow, BM128, BN128, wave64, BK_STEP1, and output ownership, but preloads all eight WNITER B-cache positions before issuing the dot loop. This tests whether a broader post-barrier B-cache LDS read window can move further toward the RADV oracle after B-pair and B-quad improved full-tile model rows. It still differs from RADV on 128 ds_load_u16_d16 sites, 128 LDS b16 stores, and the output store shape (64 global_store_b32 versus RADV 192 buffer_store_b32). Focused CPU-reference gates passed for p512 and p513 candidate-selected rows, and p33 stayed on the existing narrow routes and passed. It is rejected for production promotion because same-runner focused timing regressed badly versus the accepted BN96/BN64 packed-Q8_1 policy on large rows: p512 ffn_out 8443.89 -> 15560.60 us, ffn_gate 7574.49 -> 12631.81 us, result_output 65982.12 -> 105784.41 us; p513 ffn_out 8263.92 -> 15854.83 us, ffn_gate 7459.87 -> 14484.62 us, result_output 67232.12 -> 122643.50 us. It compiled through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=40, VGPR=196, LDS=20480, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 128 global_store_b32, and 2 barriers. This matches RADV's 32 WMMA and 64 ds_load_b64 axes and moves the store count from the accepted default's 64 to 128, but it still misses RADV's 22528-byte LDS footprint, 128 ds_load_u16_d16, 128 LDS b16 stores, and 192 buffer stores. Focused CPU-reference gates passed for p33, p512, and p513 with the candidate selected. It is rejected for production promotion because same-runner focused timing regressed every row versus the accepted default: p33 Vcur 678.53 -> 798.70 us, ffn_out 3266.17 -> 3836.85 us, result_output 17918.60 -> 23491.26 us; p512 Vcur 1229.96 -> 2383.51 us, ffn_out 22244.78 -> 28722.42 us, result_output 180519.25 -> 232795.11 us; p513 Vcur 1031.38 -> 1138.76 us, ffn_out 12337.31 -> 16923.53 us, result_output 112612.90 -> 135186.16 us. Combining the source-visible b64 load and fullstore writeback pivots is still not the Vulkan cooperative-matrix load/store/lane-ownership schedule.

The BN128 split-qsum8 packed-Q8_1 probe preserved the accepted BN128 full-column policy and changed only the qsum chunk size from 16 columns to 8 columns. This was a bounded live-range/occupancy probe after accepted BN128 split-qsum removed the old simple-BN128 spill wall. It compiled through CMake/Ninja and achieved the intended resource effect: wave32, SGPR=27, VGPR=120, LDS=4352, no spills, versus accepted BN128 split-qsum VGPR=152. Focused p33/p512/p513 CPU-reference gates passed; route traces proved p33 stayed on BN64 while p512 and p513 selected split-qsum8 under the opt-in env. Same-runner focused timing rejects it for production: p512 improved Vcur 541.25 -> 538.38 us, Qcur 1874.22 -> 1778.22 us, and ffn_out 7048.63 -> 6558.90 us, but regressed ffn_gate 6303.30 -> 6843.30 us and the dominant result_output 56355.07 -> 61269.62 us. p513 regressed every row: Vcur 537.46 -> 557.28 us, Qcur 2040.09 -> 2183.83 us, ffn_out 7958.16 -> 8170.67 us, ffn_gate 7449.29 -> 7793.47 us, and result_output 64570.31 -> 71864.74 us. Lower VGPR alone is not enough; the extra chunk-loop overhead and changed scheduling lose the rows that dominate model throughput.

The BM32/BN128 packed-Q8_1 probe preserved BN128 full-column coverage but changed output ownership from the accepted BM64/COLS32 split-qsum route to BM32/COLS16 with a simple qsum tile. This was a bounded register-tile/output-ownership test after Q8_0 remained the worst post-BN128 basket row. It compiled through CMake/Ninja with wave32, SGPR=27, VGPR=135, LDS=4352, no spills, improving compile pressure versus accepted BN128 split-qsum's VGPR=152. Focused CPU-reference gates passed for p33, p512, and p513; route traces proved p33 stayed on the narrow/default path while p512 and p513 selected the candidate under the opt-in env. Same-runner focused timing rejects it for production because every p512 and p513 row regressed versus the current default: p512 Vcur 550.04 -> 625.05 us, Qcur 1882.69 -> 2087.72 us, ffn_out 7043.92 -> 8482.13 us, ffn_gate 6416.43 -> 7242.67 us, result_output 55913.71 -> 64160.60 us; p513 Vcur 531.02 -> 717.80 us, Qcur 2018.92 -> 2432.01 us, ffn_out 7762.03 -> 9816.67 us, ffn_gate 7209.13 -> 8530.12 us, result_output 63218.36 -> 76252.10 us. Reducing per-thread columns while keeping BN128 loses row-tile amortization and does not recover the missing Vulkan schedule.

The Q8_0 VK128 buffer-store probe replaced both full-tile and guarded edge writeback with __builtin_amdgcn_raw_buffer_store_b32 while preserving the direct-F32 VK128 W64 math path and the stage-allocation LDS footprint. The original gfx1151 descriptor word 0x27000 was wrong: a CMake/Ninja-built raw-buffer-store fixture showed it effectively no-ops, while the Tensile gfx11 resource word 0x31004000 passes both make_buffer_rsrc and manual descriptors on production-sized 4096x512, 14336x512, and 128256x512 output shapes. With the route patched to use 0x31004000, focused CPU-reference gates passed for p512 and p513 selected large rows, while p33 correctly stayed on the narrow packed route. The route is still rejected for production because same-runner focused timing regressed versus current default routing on every selected large row: p512 ffn_out 7048.33 -> 10357.40 us, ffn_gate 6358.83 -> 10973.75 us, result_output 56008.26 -> 98015.71 us; p513 ffn_out 7611.67 -> 10779.03 us, ffn_gate 6875.18 -> 13367.04 us, result_output 62863.76 -> 111411.43 us. Correct raw buffer stores are therefore a necessary primitive, not the Vulkan-winning schedule. The next exact-schedule attempt must reproduce RADV's cooperative-matrix load/store lane ownership and halfword LDS topology, not just the buffer-store opcode.

The Q5_K packed-Q8_1/x4 CR issue-order probe preserved BM128/BN128/WG256/wave64/BK_STEP1 and changed only the inner dot issue order to consume one Q5 row cache across columns before advancing cr. It compiled through CMake/Ninja but spilled badly (wave64, SGPR=50, VGPR=192, LDS=10240, private_segment_fixed_size=452, vgpr_spill_count=135) while preserving 512 v_dot4_i32_iu8, 64 global_store_b32, and 2 barriers. Focused p33/p512/p513 CPU-reference gates passed; p512 selected CR for Qcur/ffn_out/ffn_gate, p33 stayed on rows2/MMQ64, and p513 fell back to current MMQL128 for tails. It is rejected because same-runner p512 focused timing regressed Qcur 1225.57 -> 3832.51 us, ffn_out 7453.69 -> 21017.01 us, and ffn_gate 7161.45 -> 19333.78 us. The issue-order axis increases live ranges/spills and should not be continued without a different B ownership/prefetch strategy.

Follow-up after the earlier rocWMMA-unavailable note found rocWMMA headers in /srv/vm-shared/rocm/rocm-7.14.0a20260610 and proved they can compile against the active /srv/vm-shared/rocm/rocm-head compiler for gfx1151 when used from scratch. A minimal default accumulator store plus f16 WMMA fixture compiled only as wave32; forcing -mwavefrontsize64 failed because the generated rocWMMA path called the wave32 WMMA builtin without the required wave32 target feature. The extracted gfx1151 code object emitted wavefront_size=32, v_wmma_f32_16x16x16_f16, global_load_b128 for A/B, and eight global_store_b32 per 16x16 accumulator wave. That default store lane map matches the existing HRX wave32 helper shape (row = lane>>4 + 2*i, col = lane&15, even accumulator elements), so it does not expose a simple lane-coordinate fix. Attempting a cooperative accumulator fragment with fragment_scheduler::coop_row_major_2d also failed at template compile time: rocWMMA reports accumulator cooperative fragments as unsupported/invalid for this path. Decision: keep this as environment and ISA evidence, not a production route. The remaining Vulkan large aligned direct-WMMA delta is still the RADV cooperative-matrix global store/load/lane-ownership lowering for the 128x128 family; source-visible HIP C++ scalar/fullstore/store-stage variants have already failed to recover it.
